name: Saint Bonaventure
history: A Franciscan theologian who taught at Paris alongside Saint Thomas Aquinas, then led the Franciscan order for seventeen years as its minister general, so wisely that he is called its second founder. He wrote the official life of Saint Francis and The Journey of the Mind into God. He is the Seraphic Doctor of the Church.
life: Giovanni di Fidanza was born at Bagnoregio near Viterbo. Tradition holds that as a child he was cured of a grave illness through the prayers of Saint Francis. He studied at Paris, joined the Franciscans, and became a master of theology at the same time as Aquinas. In 1257 he was elected minister general of an order divided between those who wanted strict poverty and those who wanted to adapt. He held it together with firmness and charity, gave it constitutions, and wrote the Major Life of Francis. His mystical works trace how all creation, rightly seen, leads the soul upward to God. Gregory X made him cardinal bishop of Albano in 1273, and the story is told that when the envoys came with his red hat he was washing dishes and asked them to hang it on a tree. He died during the Council of Lyons in 1274, which he had helped to prepare.
prayerTo: Saint Bonaventure, you studied deeply and loved more deeply still, and you saw the footprints of God in all creation. Pray for teachers and students of theology, for the Franciscan family, and for me, that my learning may lead me to prayer and my prayer to love. Amen.
penance: Take a walk today and look at created things as Bonaventure did, as traces of God, and finish whatever humble chore you would rather avoid.
meditation: He asked his readers to look at creation as a ladder to God. What in nature has drawn you towards Him?
